new_public_evidence.source: Shin, Ramdas, Rinaldo, E-detectors: A Nonparametric Framework for Sequential Change Detection
new_public_evidence.result: For bounded streams with time-varying dependent conditional means, one-step mean-test e-factors generate e-SR/e-CUSUM detectors with nonasymptotic ARL control; e-SR is recommended at the universal threshold because it dominates e-CUSUM there.

derived_results.claim: For r117 d_t in [-0.09,0.4] and a declared material threshold m, L_t=1+lambda(d_t-m)/(m+0.09), 0<lambda<1, is a conditional e-value whenever E[d_t|past]<=m. The e-SR recursion R_t=L_t(R_{t-1}+1) with threshold 1/alpha_local has ARL at least 1/alpha_local under no material weighted harm.

Local e-SR alarms should only trigger reversible shrink/fallback toward base. False local alarms then cost efficiency but do not invalidate target estimation or the cumulative r117 CS. ARL is deliberately not described as global PFA across repeated routing episodes.

For B=25/9, tolerated future excess V_tol over H raw samples maps to weighted threshold m=V_tol/(BH). Because actual mixture second-moment excess is upper-bounded by B times the weighted paired mean, this gives a conservative routing target in operational variance units.

Using r116's synthetic paired variation as an information-scale diagnostic and ARL 100k, a persistent alternative only twice a 10-variance-unit-per-100k material threshold needs roughly 145k raw samples under a small-signal optimal-log-growth approximation; a 20-unit threshold needs ~36k, while 5 units needs ~581k. The prior static harmful regime was far subtler, implying millions of samples for high-fidelity-only local detection. Sparse failure labels therefore cannot be the only fast drift-routing signal.

The emerging design cleanly separates: cumulative high-fidelity certification (r117), local high-fidelity material-harm routing with ARL semantics (r119), and cheap low-fidelity proxy/state drift routing that may react early but carries no truth-certificate semantics.

engineering_update.scope: The e-SR validity/ARL statement is theorem-level under the bounded conditional-mean setup. Delay numbers are synthetic small-signal evidence-scale diagnostics, not a nonstationary delay theorem.

negative_or_scope_evidence: Do not treat ARL as probability of never false fallback across repeated episodes.
Do not use low-fidelity proxy routing as a high-fidelity safety certificate.
The paired detector is conservative for actual mixture harm because the weighted expert average is only an upper bound on mixture second moment.
Subtle local harm can be statistically invisible on operational horizons when high-fidelity failures are rare.
frontier: Choose a declared operational materiality scale and test a predeclared lambda mixture e-SR under materially harmful abrupt regimes, plus benign false-fallback cost.
Build low-fidelity proxy-drift shrinkage toward base as a reversible routing heuristic and quantify avoided high-fidelity variance loss before local e-SR confirmation.
Jointly optimize defensive floor e for variance gain, cumulative certification speed, local harm evidence rate and maximum importance ratio.
Extend bounded paired e-SR to dependent/systematic sibling resampling and random particle counts under proper weighting.
Only after trajectory semantics are theorem-clean, build judge-guided proposal plus sparse high-fidelity truth agent evaluation.
exact_next_action: Use the three-layer separation explicitly. Pick one operational local materiality target in future variance units and instantiate a small fixed lambda mixture for the r119 e-SR; validate its delay only on regimes whose weighted harm actually exceeds that threshold. In parallel build a cheap proxy-drift rule whose permitted action is only reversible epsilon increase toward base, then measure how much variance harm it avoids before sparse high-fidelity evidence arrives. Keep all proxy routing claims separate from r117/r119 statistical guarantees.
